preamble: Before front vowels and [j], the labiodental /f/ can be replaced by a voiceless alveolo-palatal sibilant [ɕ] as the outcome of labial palatalization. This is documented in Daco-Romanian dialects: in the northern half of the Moldavian area, including Bukovina and north-eastern Bessarabia, in north-eastern Transylvania, and in Maramureș. Dialectologists transcribe the result ŝ or ś, or s with a note that it is palatal in timbre, unlike primary /s/. Guia describes it as developing through an intermediate fs' stage. Typical forms are ŝérbi for standard fierbe 'boils' and śer for fier 'iron'. The voiced v undergoes the parallel change to [ʑ]. South of the Bacău–Vaslui–Huși line, f gives the older h' stage instead, as in h'érbi.

examples.note: Recorded in Bukovina (Vicovu de Jos, Mănăstirea Humorului), where these forms coexist with fiérbi, fiert. One speaker corrected herself: fiérbi, spúnim di fapt ŝérbi 'we actually say ŝérbi'.
Recorded in many localities of Bacău, Botoșani, Iași and Suceava counties.
Recorded in the north-eastern Republic of Moldova, where f, v and ĉ give ś, ź and ś (vis > źis, nuci > nuś).
Found in a compact area of northern Sălaj county and eastern Țara Oașului. The s that comes from f has a palatal timbre, distinct from primary s.
